entry_points.name: close_account
entry_points.note: Loads the user row, calls anonymize_user and commits.

stores.name: users

erasure.note: close_account overwrites full_name with the constant string "removed", which does not carry the previous value.

fields.name: metadata_json
fields.note: The comment on the column says the value is an arbitrary key/value set by the client and that support pastes contact details into it.

erasure.note: anonymize_user writes only email and full_name; no code writes or clears metadata_json.

fields.name: deleted_at
fields.note: Soft-delete marker column on the user row.

erasure.note: The column is declared but no code in the repository sets it, and no job reads it.
close_account replaces email with its SHA-256 hash and leaves the row in place, so the row still points at the same person; no delete statement is issued anywhere in the repository.

stores.note: Table of user accounts defined with SQLAlchemy.

stores.name: tickets

fields.name: notes
fields.note: The comment on the column says the free text may contain phone numbers.

fields.name: opened_at
fields.note: Timestamp on a row carrying a foreign key to the user.

erasure.note: close_account deletes no row, and the User.tickets relationship carries no cascade argument, so the ticket rows and their columns stay as they are.

stores.note: Support tickets, each carrying a foreign key to the user.

stores.name: request_log

fields.name: ip_address
fields.note: Read from the request client host and written to the log line at middleware.py:11.

erasure.note: The deletion route touches only the user row; nothing in the repository removes or rotates the log records written by log_request.

stores.note: Python logging logger that records the client IP address and the request path for every request.
